sentences.text: An FIR was instituted against the revisionist alleging that after the death of the mother of the informant, her father along with five other siblings had started living in the house of the revisionist Masoom Raza, Advocate on rent.
The father of the revisionist started to sell dumplings and tea on the road side.
On 28.08.2023 at about 8 P.M. when the father of the informant was at his shop, the revisionist is stated to have barged into the room of the informant and was committing sexual assault on her.
In the meantime, the father of the informant reached there and on seeing the said act, the revisionist and the father of the victim entered into an altercation which ended in a physical brawl.
5. The revisionist is stated to have taken the father of the informant to some unknown place and put him to death.
The dead body had been sent for postmortem.

The revisionist was even seen by the informant fondling with her younger daughter also and she was threatened by the revisionist to refrain her from telling anybody about it, otherwise her brothers and sisters would be put to death.
The FIR was instituted on 05.09.2023.

Arguments for Revisionist:
6. It is argued that the deceased person who is the father of the informant was admitted in the emergency of the hospital on 28.08.2023 at 6.26 P.M.

He has stated that the deceased expired on 31.08.2023 and the inquest proceedings was undertaken by the police at 16.35 P.M. on 31.08.2023 and the information to the police station was sent by the informant herein which finds mention in the inquest report which has been filed as Annexure No. 4 to the Criminal Revision.
The informant is Panch Witness No. 3 in the said inquest report.

It is further stated that in the statement of the informant under Section 161 Cr.P.C., she has categorically stated that some unknown persons had got her signatures on a blank paper as she was not in best of her mental status and she along with other family members was living in the house of the revisionist for about six years.
The allegations made against the revisionist are false.

7. It is further argued that subsequent to it, the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and she has reiterated the statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and has also stated that the revisionist has not committed any offence with her or any member of the family and her father had consumed some poison out of depression.
As such, he has expired.
Subsequent to it an amount of Rs. 9 lakhs was recovered from the house of the informant and the police alleged that the said amount was given by the revisionist to the informant to keep mum.

8. Learned counsel for the revisionist has stated that another statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
was recorded on 12.09.2023 of the victim and therein she has reiterated the allegations leveled in the FIR and she has also added the fact that the said Rs. 9 lakhs were given to her by the revisionist Masoom Raza Rahi @ Rahi Masoom Raza vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199580222/
2 and asked her to keep silent.

entities.text: Masoom Raza Rahi @ Rahi Masoom Raza vs State Of Up And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said bag containing the amount of Rs. 9 lakhs has been handed over to the police.
The said subsequent statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has been recorded after tutoring and legal consultation.
The revisionist is a practicing Advocate at the civil court and the instant case has been foisted on him by his political rivals as the revisionist is a sympathizer and a member of the ruling party.
The said amount of Rs. 9 lakhs does not belong to him and has been planted by his political rivals.

Arguments for State:
9.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the Criminal Revision on the ground that the said order for framing of charge is a detailed order and has been passed after proper application of mind.

In addition to it,
the charge have been framed by the court concerned on 17.01.2024.
Learned A.G.A. has further stated that at the stage of framing of charge, prima facie material has to be taken into account only and Court has to consider the prosecution story as a whole to be true.
If no case is made out then only accused person can be discharged.

10. Herein the matter is a replica of the case of Zahira Habibulla H. Sheikh and Another Vs. State of Gujarat and Others reported at (2004) 4 Supreme Court Cases 158, wherein the victim was coerced to enter into a compromise and herein heavy amount of Rs. 9 lakhs has been recovered from the possession of the victim.

entities.text: Zahira Habibulla H. Sheikh and Another Vs. State of Gujarat and Others reported at (2004) 4 Supreme Court Cases 158
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such a heavy amount of money cannot be planted by anybody and the same cannot be found from the possession of informant who comes from poor financial background.

Conclusion:
11.

After hearing the parties and taking into consideration that the name of the revisionist finds mention in the subsequent statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and also the fact that a heavy amount of Rs. 9 lakhs has been recovered from the possession of the victim herein which has not been properly explained, I do not find any illegality in the order of framing of charge and subsequent framing of charge against the applicant.
12. As such, the instant Criminal Revision is found devoid of merits and is rejected.
